issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Course initializer with parameters labeled (name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) and even show example usage Course(name: ..., instructor: ..., ratings: ...). However the solution's Course initializer uses a different parameter ordering/labels (init(instructor: String, name: String, ratings: [Int])). This label/order mismatch between template/problem and solution can confuse students when they compare their implementation to the provided solution or example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course initializer parameter labels and order consistent across all artifacts. For example, change the solution initializer to init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) so it matches the problem statement and the template (or alternatively update the problem statement and template to match the chosen signature).

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an initializer labeled as Course(name:..., instructor:..., ratings:...), but the solution's Course initializer declares parameters in a different order (init(instructor: String, name: String, ratings: [Int])). This divergence in parameter ordering for the same conceptual initializer can confuse students when mapping the example usage in the problem to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's Course initializer use the same parameter label order as the problem and template: change the initializer signature to init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) (or alternatively update all call sites to use the same label order) so students can directly map the example Course(name:..., instructor:..., ratings:...) to the implementation.
